features.text: Martha is a 50-year-old female with a past medical history significant for congestive heart failure, depression, and hypertension.
Martha has been traveling a lot recently due to lighter circumstances and has received her vaccine.
Martha has been hiking, including a trip to the Northern Cascades around Mount Baker.
Martha has been resisting salty foods such as tater tots and soft pretzels as part of her low sodium diet.
Martha has not experienced chest pains, shortness of breath, or swelling in her legs.
Martha has been attending weekly therapy sessions for the past year.
Martha has not had any thoughts of self-harm or harm to others.
Martha has been forgetting to take her blood pressure medication, especially during stressful times at work.
Martha's work has been stressful with long hours and late nights, particularly with fiscal year-end data.
Martha has nasal congestion due to fall pollen and allergies.
Martha has no nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain.
Martha's blood pressure is elevated during the office visit.
Martha has a 3/6 systolic ejection murmur on heart examination.
Martha has 1+ pitting edema in her lower extremities.
Martha's echocardiogram from last year showed a low pumping function of the heart at about 45% and mitral regurgitation.
Martha's lipid panel from last year showed slightly elevated cholesterol.
Martha is currently on medications for congestive heart failure, depression, and hypertension.
Martha is being advised to increase her lisinopril to 40 mg/day and start lasix 20 mg/day.
Martha prefers to take all her pills at the same time of day.
